intro: At the very end of a sentence, って is a quotation with the verb of saying left off. It marks the words as not your own: either you pass on what someone said ("apparently", "he says"), you echo what you just heard ("you're what?"), or you repeat yourself with impatience ("I said ...!").

skills.rule: End a casual sentence with って (だって after a noun) to pass on what you heard: "apparently", "they say"; with a rising tone it echoes what you just heard.
skills.explain:
Hearsay: 明日は雨だって (apparently it'll rain tomorrow), 田中さん、来られないって (Tanaka says he can't come). The information is someone else's; って flags it as reported. Use the plain form: verbs and い-adjectives take って directly (来るって, 高いって); nouns and な-adjectives keep だ (休みだって, 静かだって). んだって is very common: 引っ越すんだって (I hear she's moving). ですって is a softer, more feminine polite form.

With a rising tone, って echoes or questions what was just said: 結婚するって? (you're getting married?!). After your own words, with a falling, firm tone, it insists: だから、行かないって (I told you, I'm not going).

って is casual. In polite or formal speech, report hearsay with そうです: 田中さんは休むそうです. Sentence-initial だって ("but", "because") is a different word.
patterns: だから、[plain form] って  "I told you"

examples.jp: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]だ{って}。
examples.en: Apparently it's going to rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さん、今日[きょう]は来[こ]られない{って}。
examples.en: Tanaka says he can't come today.

examples.jp: 駅前[えきまえ]に新[あたら]しいカフェができたんだ{って}。
examples.en: I hear a new café has opened by the station.

examples.jp: あの映画[えいが]、すごく面白[おもしろ]い{って}。
examples.en: People say that film is really good.

examples.jp: え、会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]める{って}?
だから、一人[ひとり]で大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だ{って}。
examples.en: I told you, I'm fine on my own.

contrast.note: よ hands over information as your own: 明日は雨だよ (it'll rain tomorrow, I'm telling you). って marks it as heard from someone else: 明日は雨だって (apparently).
っけ asks yourself or the listener to remind you: 会議は三時だっけ? (the meeting's at three, wasn't it?). って reports what someone told you: 会議は三時だって (they say the meeting's at three).
かな is your own wondering: 雨かな (I wonder if it'll rain). って is no guess; it relays a source: 雨だって.

mistakes.bad: 部長[ぶちょう]、田中[たなか]さんは今日[きょう]休[やす]む{って}。
mistakes.good: 部長[ぶちょう]、田中[たなか]さんは今日[きょう]休[やす]むそうです。
mistakes.note: って is casual. To a superior, report hearsay with そうです.

skills.tip: Could you add "..., someone said" (or "..., I said!") to the English? Then って.
